rubric.title: Deep learning architecture
rubric.detail: a. Diagram   b. Explanation   c. Novelty proposed   d. Time and space complexity
evidence: (a,b) Deck slides 22–23: layer-by-layer diagrams and design rationale for both BiLSTM and 1D CNN.
(c) Deck slide 17.4 states the novelty as the controlled single-variable comparison and the shared landmark front-end — and states explicitly what is NOT claimed as novel.
(d) Deck slide 17.3: big-O time, critical path, MAC counts, parameter and activation complexity for both models.
The complexity is derived in scripts/analyze_complexity.py, which asserts its parameter counts against the trained checkpoints — 2,665,477 and 736,773 both match torch exactly.
rubric.note: The novelty is stated narrowly on purpose. Claiming a new architecture would not survive the first question, because none was designed; the defensible contribution is the experiment.

rubric.title: Algorithm procedure, step by step, mathematically
evidence: Deck slides 17.1 and 17.2: a ten-step numbered derivation from webcam frame to predicted label.
Steps 1–6 cover landmark extraction, concatenation, temporal resampling, wrist-origin translation, shoulder-width scaling and z-scoring with train-split-only statistics.
Steps 7–9 give the LSTM gate and cell equations beside the 1D convolution and pooling equations, side by side.
Step 10 is the shared head: dropout, GELU, softmax, argmax — plus the label-smoothed cross-entropy objective.
Every equation is the one implemented in preprocess.py and models.py, not a textbook restatement.
rubric.note: Laying both models out against shared steps 1–6 and 10 is what shows the comparison is controlled: only 7–9 differ.

rubric.title: Hyperparameter details table with justification
evidence: Deck slides 24–25: the table and the tuning discussion.
Values are the ones actually used: AdamW, cosine annealing, label smoothing 0.05, early stopping patience 20, lr 3e-3, batch 32, 60 epochs.
Best epochs are recorded: 41/60 for BiLSTM, 45/60 for CNN.

rubric.title: Results and discussion
rubric.detail: Tables, graphs, inference achieved from the architecture.
evidence: Deck slide 27: nine metrics, both models, with a stated winner and observation per row.
Numbers are measured on a 642-clip held-out test split, not estimated.
The Research page in this app reads the same comparison.json off disk, so it cannot drift from the deck.

rubric.title: Dataset chosen, and the novelty in the dataset
evidence: Deck slides 13, 18–21: INCLUDE described, plus extraction results.
Real counts: 261 classes, 4,276 usable clips after filtering classes with fewer than 5 recordings.
Canonical sources verified: Zenodo record 4010759 (the 56.8 GB video release), the Hugging Face mirror ai4bharat/INCLUDE, and the ACM MM 2020 paper doi:10.1145/3394171.3413528.

Dataset novelty: INCLUDE is the largest published lexical ISL corpus, recorded with experienced signers rather than crowd-sourced, which is why it supports 261 classes where most ISL work reports on 20–50.
missing: A decision on the IEEE Dataport requirement — see the note.
rubric.note: Checked: INCLUDE is NOT on IEEE Dataport. It is distributed via Zenodo (record 4010759) and Hugging Face, and published at ACM Multimedia 2020. Ask your faculty whether the Zenodo DOI satisfies the requirement. IEEE DataPort does host other ISL datasets (e.g. ISL-50), so if the Dataport URL is non-negotiable, the honest options are to cite one of those as a secondary dataset or to change datasets — not to invent a link.
